status: exploratory development run; fixed before inference
question: With the compressor and decoder frozen, can a zero-initialised residual adapter on the latents make the decoder use the one-versus-two burst cue that a linear readout already finds?
stimuli: count_evidence.py prepare, identical to phase2/count-evidence-v1/pairs.json (ESC-50 fold-5 sources, 50 pairs, 25 source groups)
question_text: Are there two separate bursts of sound with a quiet gap between them?
compressor: runs/c-k16-s17-audio/compressor.pt, retrained locally with A's command (seed 17, 192 steps)

adapter.form: x + W2 gelu(W1 LayerNorm(x)), W2 zero-initialised, applied to every latent row

split: 5 folds over source groups, seed 17; adapters never see held-out groups
primary_metric: pair both-correct rate averaged over the two option orders, adapter minus base, group bootstrap 95% interval (seed 29, 10000 draws)
decision: A gain counts only if its interval excludes zero and the adapter's held-out answers follow donor latents rather than the original labels; K16 versus full/pool16 tells whether the adapter reads compressed evidence or teaches the task
controls: donor latents from another held-out source group
fresh_val 340-question regression with each fold's adapter
deviations: torch 2.7.1+cu128 instead of 2.5.1+cu121 (Blackwell GPUs); baseline scores agree with count-evidence-v1/full.csv in sign on 100/100 clips, max |diff| 0.125 logit
K16 checkpoint retrained locally: held-out 53/64 as in A's run, 62/64 identical predictions
